title: USMNT’s Johnny Cardoso nets stunning goal as Atletico Madrid advances in Champions League
content:
With the penultimate window before Mauricio Pochettino selects his United States World Cup squad, U.S. men’s national team midfielder Johnny Cardoso thrust himself back on the radar with an emphatic finish on the club game’s biggest stage.

Cardoso scored a spectacular long-range goal on Tuesday, which helped Atlético Madrid advance into the last 16 of the Champions League. The New Jersey native’s moment of skill came 48 minutes in against Club Brugge to break a 1-1 draw at the time. With the first leg of their knockout playoff level at 3-3, Cardoso’s goal wound up being the winner, though the hero was Norwegian striker Alexander Sørloth, whose hat trick secured the 4-1 win on the day (7-4 on aggregate). Atlético Madrid will now face either Liverpool or Tottenham in the next stage of the competition.

For Cardoso, it was the first Champions League goal of his career, and his first for the side he joined in the summer in a €30 million (£25.5m; $34.8m) deal from Real Betis. The emphatic strike off the bounce into the bottom left corner ended a 10-month wait for him to hit the back of the net, with his last goal coming in April 2025 during a league game for Betis.

With 22 USMNT appearances under his belt, Cardoso will hope for at least two more, with upcoming friendlies against Belgium and Portugal in Atlanta next month. His last outing for the U.S. was as a substitute in a 2-1 Concacaf Gold Cup win over Haiti last June, and he plays a position where he’s contending with the likes of Tyler Adams, Tanner Tessmann, Cristian Roldan, Sebastian Berhalter and others for a roster spot.

Meanwhile, Cardoso’s U.S. teammate Malik Tillman was absent from Bayer Leverkusen’s knockout playoff second leg against Olympiakos on Tuesday with an ankle injury.

The 23-year-old picked up the knock in Saturday’s 1-0 defeat to Union Berlin, and Leverkusen head coach Kasper Hjulmand said in a Monday press conference that “it doesn’t look good” for the American’s chances of playing in the Champions League tie. Leverkusen advanced without him, drawing 0-0 on the day to secure a 2-0 aggregate triumph and a last-16 date against either Bayern Munich or Arsenal.

Other U.S. internationals seeking a place in the last 16 via the knockout playoff round include Weston McKennie (Juventus trails Galatasaray 5-2 after the first leg), Yunus Musah (Atalanta trails Dortmund 2-0) and Folarin Balogun (Monaco trails PSG 3-2).
